launches.tagline: We help retailers sell clean energy products by using government & utility rebates to offer dramatically lower prices at checkout
launches.body:
# tl;dr

Upfront helps merchants that sell clean energy products by turning billions of dollars of rebates into dramatically lower prices at checkout. Instead of filling out paperwork and waiting 6 months for a check, our software instantly applies rebates and manages the settlement in the background.

# The Problem

Clean energy products have higher upfront costs while competing in markets defined by the importance of affordability (e.g. 60% of appliances are financed). Rebates are designed to offset these higher costs, but because rebates are complicated and not surfaced during buying decisions, consumers today choose products that are worse for both the environment and their wallets.

# The Solution

We solve this problem by partnering with retailers to enable them to transform government and utility rebates into dramatically lower prices for their customers. This solution saves consumers money, increases retailer sales, and helps deploy rebates faster than ever.

Starting with EV Chargers, we qualify consumers for all applicable rebate programs in real-time and advance their savings at checkout. After purchase, we work with the consumer to process the rebate and manage the settlement with the rebate issuer.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=69740&key=user_uploads/1202385/15a9b94d-59cc-4ebd-9cd8-2e27ba1df34a)

# The Team

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=69740&key=user_uploads/1202385/124cba11-ebdf-48b4-b7c4-56a3fa67421a)

We’ve both spent the last half decade helping merchants grow their businesses. Andrew was an engineer at Affirm, building servicing and payment systems scaling to billions of dollars in GMV. Thomas launched and GM’d markets for DoorDash both domestically and abroad. 

As new homeowners we were both struggling to figure out what rebates were available and how they actually worked… and we’d spent weeks researching climate tech! Fellow consumers and retailers agreed, so in January of 2023, we started Upfront.

We're determined to help make clean energy products the obvious choice for consumers to stamp out the nearly 1 gigaton of CO2E emitted from America’s 124 million homes annually.

launches.title: Feldy: Field-first AI for home services and contractors.
launches.tagline: Jobsite capture, 3D building scans, estimates and field documentation in one simple app.
launches.body:
**TL;DR** 👋

Feldy is field-first AI for home service companies. It unifies jobsite capture, 3D building scans, estimates, and field documentation in one simple app.

We’ve grown to over 200 paying customers on the web over the last few months, and are now launching the mobile app so field teams can use the full product on site.

Zayne and Shelby are construction software veterans with a combined 10+ years building computer vision and spatial AI tools.

**Meet Feldy:**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W0lEF7isKg4>

**The Problem:**

The biggest problem in residential home services in 2026 is still remarkably simple: estimates do not go out fast enough to homeowners.

An estimate is the quote a homeowner receives explaining what work will be done and how much it will cost. Yet, if you call a window contractor, or painter, it can still take two or three days, often longer, to receive one. Over the last 8 months, my home became a test bed for remodeling projects, and this is one of the few truths that persisted. This problem appears in nearly every trade we encountered.

_So why so long?_

The surprising part is that many of these estimates are not inherently complicated.

Consider a typical window and door contractor. A sales representative drives to the property, walks through the home, identifies every window and door, photographs existing conditions, and asks discovery questions:

* Do you want to replace the trim?
* Should the opening change?

Capturing this information can easily consume most of a one- or two-hour appointment. By the time the rep understands the property and records everything the office needs, there is _very little time left_ to actually sell the project. This is the primary reason quotes arrive days later, or require a second visit.

Furthermore, existing software makes the problem worse.

Most contractor tools have always been structured like digital forms. The software records what the estimator has already figured out, but it does very little to help figure out the job.

This is what led us to ask: what does this contractor world look like if the software recorded and figured out the job at once? Well, that’s Feldy.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110395&key=user_uploads/1494934/6bdd00aa-4517-41c6-897e-517110044d2b)

**So how do we solve this?**

Instead of requiring the person in the field to manually observe and organize everything, Feldy uses in-house computer vision and vision-language models to perform much of this _low-value work_: necessary technical work that consumes the majority of the job visit time, but creates little visible value for the homeowner.

The contractor _captures_ the property via photos/videos, lidar scans, or job walkthroughs (video and audio are combined). Feldy then interprets the capture and helps turn it into an estimate amongst a host of other workflow items such as inspection reports, proposals, materials lists, etc.

The entire thesis behind Feldy can be summed up as:

_How do we remove the time-consuming thinking required from the estimator that creates little visible value for the homeowner?_

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110395&key=user_uploads/1494934/060ca1ad-5038-40a5-868f-fb14eb04b164)

**The Scale of the bottleneck**

Angi’s list has estimated that American households undertake more than 700 million home projects annually.

Using 600 million estimates (aggressive case):

* 600M estimates \* 3.5 hours = 2.1 billion total labor hours
* 50% spent on measuring, documenting, takeoff, and estimate construction = 1.05 billion hours
* At $45–50 fully loaded cost = $47–53 billion in annual labor capacity tied up in that work

If Feldy reclaims 1–1.25 hours per estimate:

* 750 million hours returned
* Roughly $27–37 billion in productive capacity per year.

For the average home-services company, this is equivalent to reclaiming $50,000–$100,000+ in capacity each year, capacity that can be converted directly into more estimates, lower overhead, and higher revenue.

**The Team**

Zayne and Shelby met at UC Berkeley’s engineering school nearly 10 years ago. For the last three years, they have worked side by side building technology for the construction and home-services industries.

Together, they previously took a construction-software company from zero to $500k ARR in months. 

The pair is more excited than ever to build the next generation of software for home-service businesses.

**The ask**

If you know anyone who works in home services, tell them about Feldy and ask them to download the app!

Search Feldy AI on [IOS ](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/feldy-ai/id6780327228)and [Android ](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.feldy.app)app stores.

launches.title: Aether  - AI platform for rooftop solar
launches.tagline: Aether is AI design and workflow software for solar installers.
launches.body:
**TL;DR**

[Aether](https://aetherenergie.com/) offers an AI-powered end-to-end platform for rooftop solar installers. We combine advancements in computer vision/lidar and LLMs to bring a unique workflow automation tool for solar installers worldwide.

## Before we start, a sneak peek at Aether:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79053&key=user_uploads/1527633/4dd1fd38-1a6f-42f1-b8b8-1ad5d62ea174)

## Some Background

---

Hey all, we’re [Shelby Bons](https://linkedin.com/in/shelby-bons-ucberkeley) and [Zayne Sagar](https://linkedin.com/in/zaynesager), two climate entrepreneurs! Our fundamental mission is to make rooftop solar energy accessible and cheap throughout the world.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79053&key=user_uploads/1527633/561a67f7-4f40-419e-af7f-2ff7557ac5b7)

For rooftop solar to be deployed, it’s really up to solar installers. To us, the people who run these companies are our heroes. Last year we spoke to hundreds of solar installers and one thing is clear - they don’t have the tools to make them successful. We reimagined rooftop solar software from the ground up for them.

Aether _automates the boring stuff for solar installers using AI_.

## **❌** The Problem:

The biggest problem in US rooftop solar is still solar soft costs. These are non-hardware costs associated with a solar project, and they amount to north of 60% of the total solar cost of an installed system! If you reduce this you create more demand for rooftop solar in the market = better outcome for our planet.

**Contributors to high soft costs:**

* **PV CAD Design teams still manually build rooftop PV site designs**. This is time-consuming and prone to lots of errors. Mistakes here mean re-doing plansets and permitting which can cost $1k - $2k extra.
* **Almost all solar design tools are inaccurate in production and consumption modeling**. This is what tells rooftop owners “Is this the right investment for me?” Most solar tools were built as a sidekick for sales reps, with just enough basic estimates to sell a solar proposal. Consumers are smarter now and recent legal litigations are forcing better modeling to be done when selling solar.
* **Dependency on multiple platforms:** Most solar companies use a software stack of 6 - 10 point solutions. Collectively the solution is dumb and creates chaotic workflows where deals get lost and project delays happen a lot. This is very expensive.
* **Lack of project visibility across teams** causing lost sales deals, and project delays

We estimate $5k to $ 7k added soft costs for a typical rooftop project occurring because of the above.

## **✅** Solution:

**Aether is built to streamline the rooftop solar workflow end to end. Think Procore or Veeva but for Solar with an AI twist.**

With Aether, solar companies can rapidly generate PV site designs, sell using a beautiful PV proposal, and then manage it to installation in one simplified workflow.

Aether is made up of hubs that help specific roles in a solar installation company do their job, but more importantly, collaborate with other teams as needed with the help of AI.

**Our two core innovations:**

* We built an in-house computer vision model.
* We also decided to build a mini fine-tuned model for solar. Being trained on items such as system production data, vision model outputs, etc. (Can’t give the rest of our sauce away!)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79053&key=user_uploads/1527633/a0dc44ab-bc4f-498d-bc2d-7318a4751d70)

**The result is a unified AI platform to streamline solar with solar agents.**

[Aether Platform - Sneak Peak](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EFJuKOI8kEs&feature=youtu.be)

**💲Opportunity:** Aether will be a big player in the young and emerging Solar software vertical, which has a projected 20B Global TAM up for grabs by 2025.

## About Us

_Shelby and Zayne met at UC Berkeley close to a decade ago both originally being born in complete opposite ends of the world, France and Fiji._

_Shelby studied Materials Science and Engineering at UC Berkeley and was briefly headed for a Ph.D. in Theoretical Physics before founding Aether. She has worked at Dolby Laboratories, Voltaiq, and Sunrun in Data Science & Machine Learning roles._

_Zayne had brief stints at multiple climate-driven companies, working on problems around space-based weather data and energy modeling problems at the intersection of software. He has built high-performing product & engineering teams from the ground up by the age of 28._

Residential contractors provide a critical service to our economy: building and maintaining the supply of housing. Unfortunately, those businesses are still operated in an incredibly manual way. A significant portion of that cost is attributed to the office work involved with finding, coordinating, and managing those small jobs. [**Drillbit**](https://www.drillbit.com) allows contractors to be entirely hands-off, enabling them to focus 100% of their time on their core business. launches.body:
**TLDR:** Every year, consumers miss out on more than **$50B** because they are not claiming the money they are entitled to. We built AI agents that claim it for them.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=83836&key=user_uploads/1984796/7093e028-b7ff-4ac4-9942-f98c49b9d002)

# The Problem 🚩

When stuff you’ve already bought goes on sale or when flights you’ve booked are delayed, policies entitle you to money. But spotting these opportunities and claiming the cash you’re owed is time-consuming and confusing. Industries subject to such policies include retail, airlines, hotels, technology, and even the government.

# Our Solution 💸

We're building AI that connects to your email inbox to: scan your e-receipts, identify opportunities to get you dollars, and automatically claim them by contacting customer service via email, phone, forms, or chat.

We started by automating refunds in the shopping industry and have secured $6,650, growing **233% MoM**. With AI, we've been able to generalize that same automation to tackle refunds in the flight industry and the class-action lawsuit landscape. That’s when we understood why this had never been done before…

# Why now? 🚨

AI enables us, for the first time, to automatically:

1. **Reason about unstructured data at scale**
2. **Handle complex, nuanced customer service interactions**

 

Generalizing securing refunds from one industry to all industries turns each step of the process into an unstructured data processing problem. For example, having a parser that can only understand Cotsco receipts and a scraper that can only read the price from the Costco website is not enough anymore: you need a parser that can understand changing receipts from all enterprises and a scraper that can read information from any website. The ability to reason about unstructured data at scale replaces the rigid, static software, solving the issue.

### In short, PAP! represents an opportunity to finally realize the dream customer journey — sign up once, forget we exist, and earn money effortlessly.

### **The Problem**

Property management operations are relentless, high-stakes, hands-on work built on relationships with owners, tenants, and vendors that take years to earn and seconds to lose.

It's overwhelmingly manual: **roughly 90% of the work is still manual** and extremely labor-intensive with **89% of property management companies outsourcing work** to teams overseas.

About half of leasing inquiries come in at night and on weekends, when no one's answering. **Conversion drops 7x after the first hour**.

Unresolved work orders are a top reason tenants don't renew, and **every lost renewal costs thousands** once you count turn and vacancy.

The work is rules-based and repetitive, but it demands constant attention, and missing any single step breaks the chain. That's why these roles scale so badly with headcount— you're paying for someone to be awake at the right moment to do menial tasks.

---

## **Our Solution**

**Maintenance Coordination Agent** Takes a maintenance request from submission to resolution:

* **Intake across any channel** — captures requests from email, SMS, and tenant portals, normalizing them into a single queue
* **Intelligent triage** — applies a proprietary relative and objective scoring algorithm to prioritize and triage issues in real time as conditions change
* **Smart dispatch** — routes to the right vendor based on trade, availability, and cost, sends the dispatch, and tracks confirmation
* **Persistent follow-up** — chases vendors, tenants, and owners intelligently until the job is on track and on schedule
* **Repair verification** — confirms work was actually completed via tenant sign-off, photo evidence, and vendor confirmation before closing the loop
* **Invoice processing** — validates invoices against the scope of work and approved estimates, flags discrepancies, and routes for payment approval

* **Smart routing** — matches each lead to the right unit, schedules the tour, sends the application, and tracks completion
* **Document analysis** — reviews submitted IDs, pay stubs, and bank statements, flagging income, completeness, and inconsistencies against your criteria
* **Verification & screening** — runs identity verification and background/credit screening, then compiles a clean, decision-ready file
* **Persistent follow-up** — chases prospects intelligently until they're marked qualified

**What makes us different than traditional PMS systems?**

* We handle can handle edge cases proactively, asking for more information, reading documents, and determining the best course of action
* We don’t automate reply drafts, we send out messages, dispatch calls, retrieve missing information, and push stalled work-orders or application processes to completion.

Hey YC! 👋

We’re [Luca](https://www.linkedin.com/in/luca-hadife/) and [Hosny](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mohamed-hosny-hussein/), founders of [Kebra](https://kebra.com/?utm_source=ycombinator&utm_medium=launch&utm_campaign=yc_launch_2026).

## TL;DR

Kebra makes the field queryable.

We capture what happens across jobs, sites, and assets and turn it into a live operating memory that AI can query and act on. Our AI employees use that context to automate the work that follows across the systems companies already use.

Every job makes that memory richer, building the company specific context software agents use today and physical agents will need tomorrow.

We’re already working with field operations companies across Florida, Pennsylvania, and California.

<https://youtu.be/VIwv5iVm8Ok>

## The problem

Field operations never got their Claude Code moment.

We spent months inside HVAC companies trying to automate their back office. We built AI employees for claims, reporting, coordination, and follow ups.

They kept breaking.

Not because the AI could not do the work, but because it was acting on a reality that never happened. The most important part of the operation happened on the ground and was never properly captured.

A missing serial number. A photo never taken. What the technician actually found stuck in their head.

You cannot automate an alternate reality. Before AI can operate the field, the field has to become queryable.

## Our Solution

Kebra makes field operations queryable.

**Capture what happens:** Field teams document jobs through photos, voice, video, and structured workflows. Kebra checks what is missing while they are still on site.

**Build the operating memory:** Every job updates a live history of sites, assets, repairs, decisions, and how the company actually works.

**AI employees act on it:** They use that context to automate reports, claims, coordination, compliance, follow ups, and other back office work across the systems the company already uses.

## Vision

Every job makes Kebra’s operating memory richer.

Today, software agents use that context to automate field operations. Tomorrow, physical AI and robots will need the same company specific context to understand each site, asset, procedure, and history before they can work autonomously.

Kebra is building the context layer for field operations.

**Bernard is building the AI front and back office for home and commercial appliance servicers.**

They manage each repair from the first customer call through scheduling, dispatch, diagnosis, parts preparation, technician handoff, and follow-up. Bernard works across phone, text, email, warranty feeds, and existing field-service systems, carrying the job context across every surface.

We are already live in the field with some of the largest authorized service companies in the country.

Our goal is simple: make the first visit the last one.\
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eiGjkYMeu2k>

### The first truck roll should not be a diagnostic visit

Appliance repair is an information and inventory problem. A technician cannot simply carry washer parts. The exact appliance, model, revision, symptoms, and failure mode determine which parts might be required, and many nearly identical parts are not interchangeable.

When that information does not come together before the appointment, the first visit becomes a diagnostic visit. The technician identifies the failure, orders the part, and returns days later to complete the repair. Customers wait longer, technicians complete fewer jobs, and servicers lose capacity and margin.

### Pre-ID prepares the repair before the truck rolls

When a customer reports that their washer will not drain, Bernard does more than book an appointment.

Bernard identifies the exact appliance, asks follow-up questions specific to the symptoms, and collects missing evidence from the customer. Pre-ID then combines that information with repair history, similar completed visits, manufacturer guidance, parts data, and the servicer’s own operating knowledge.

Before the visit, Bernard gives the technician a diagnosis, ranked parts, the most useful next questions, and the evidence supporting each recommendation. The office can prepare the parts, confirm they will arrive on time, and hand the technician a complete picture of the job.

Every interaction and completed repair feeds back into Bernard, turning the servicer’s daily work into shared knowledge.

### Why start with the servicer?

Every appliance company makes a promise at the point of sale. The servicer is the person who ultimately has to keep that promise inside someone’s home or business.

That visit affects the customer, the retailer, the manufacturer, the warranty company, and the parts distributor. Yet the servicer coordinating it is often working across disconnected phone systems, inboxes, scheduling tools, parts catalogs, and knowledge held by a few experienced employees.

We believe that building the world’s most efficient appliance servicers will create happier customers and a more connected appliance ecosystem.

Bernard starts with the servicer because that is where the industry meets the physical world.

[Dan Katzman](https://www.linkedin.com/in/dankatzman/) previously helped build Nava Benefits' strategy and operations team, working across the product and operational infrastructure required to deliver a complicated, service-heavy experience reliably, while also leading partnerships. Before Nava, he invested at City Light Capital and Golub Capital.

Before that, he worked on RPA and cognitive automation at Disney, before enterprise automation was cool.

**TL;DR:** Title insurance is the thorn in the side of every single residential real estate transaction in America. With the home market bleeding, you'll find attorneys processing documents by hand with outdated software at title agencies. Vestris automates the back office and supplements processors the way software should — _letting shops give the same care to closing the biggest purchase of a buyer's life._

<https://youtu.be/u2do97AOvQY?si=JB78OAx5hDp80PXT>

### The Problem

Imagine you're shopping the market and you just found your dream home. You're ready to purchase, the contract is signed, everything is in place.

And you're recommended a settlement company, and told to buy title insurance.

Most homeowners couldn't tell you what title insurance actually buys them. In a nutshell: **you're paying for the peace of mind that the property you're buying has no open claims against it** — payments a title company makes on your behalf.

But it's also a process that takes weeks. Behind the phone, you've got lawyers processing files, manually checking emails, and scanning two seemingly identical documents for changes.

Meanwhile, the incumbent software is a decade-old, per-file database whose premium plans put it out of reach for the small and mid-size shops that make up most of the market.

### The Solution

Vestris runs the file end to end:

**Reads everything on arrival** — every document that hits a processor's inbox is routed to the right order, new contracts spin up new files, and the routine back-and-forth is handled, so the first 30% of a file is done before a human even looks.

**Does the math** — logs into county tax and land portals to pull up-to-date figures, then prorates taxes, utilities, HOA dues, and special assessments to the settlement date on that county's convention, every figure traced back to its source.

**Drafts the commitment** — building Schedule A from the vesting and legal description and Schedule B from the exceptions in the record, the work a small shop waits a week and pays an abstractor hundreds for.

**Closes it out** — reconciling the closing disclosure against the settlement statement, handling the lender back-and-forth, and showing the processor exactly what changed, so no one's squinting at two seemingly identical PDFs.

Every step still goes through human approval. What changes is bandwidth: **a mom-and-pop shop never has to turn down an order because they're swamped**, and they get to spend their time on the in-person care that made buyers seek them out in the first place.

### The Team

We're Aahil and Josh, best friends and UMich roommates.

Aahil previously built SafeKids and holds three USPTO patents. He spent the summer closing files at a title shop, seeing the processor's grind firsthand.

Josh previously built live-telemetry and communication systems for Michigan's Formula SAE team. He worked the same title desk, and stole the cubicle with the monitor 😠

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109429&key=user_uploads/3411947/af48be0b-23b2-4cb5-9c1c-4eb5c7b45e50)

### Our Ask

We're running Vestris in parallel at a title shop that settles millions in deals a month.

If you know anyone at **a title agency, escrow, or settlement company** — we'd love an intro.

And if you've ever bought or sold a home, reach out! You probably have strong feelings about the title process :)

You can reach us at [founders@vestris.ai](mailto:founders@vestris.ai), or better yet, give us a call at +1 (571) 466 7878.
